questions.q: What is the best structure for a stakeholder summary of an analysis?
options: Methods first, then a long list of every test, then the result at the end
Only the p-value
Answer first, then the evidence, then the caveats, then a recommendation
Only a chart with no text
questions.explain: Stakeholders want the conclusion first, then just enough evidence to trust it, the limits of the analysis, and what to do next.

questions.q: In the churn chart, the two groups' 95% error bars overlap slightly, yet the test on the difference was significant. What should you conclude?
options: The test must be wrong
Overlapping individual intervals do not by themselves mean the difference is unreal; report the interval for the difference
The intervals should never overlap in any valid chart
The sample size is too small
questions.explain: The question is about the difference, and the correct uncertainty for that is the interval on the difference, not whether two separate intervals touch.

questions.q: Why does the results table include the spend outcome even though it was not significant?
options: Because a non-significant result is proof of no effect
Because it makes the table longer
It should be removed, since only significant results matter
Because honest reporting includes every pre-planned outcome, not just the ones that worked
questions.explain: Reporting all planned outcomes prevents selective reporting. A non-significant result means no detectable effect, not proof of zero effect.

questions.q: Which is a good practice when packaging the project for a portfolio?
options: Include a README, seeded scripts, the results table, the chart, and a clear note that the data is simulated
Only include a screenshot of the p-value
Present the data as if it were real customers
Omit the code so the reader cannot check it
questions.explain: A reproducible project with clear documentation and honest labeling of simulated data is what reviewers can trust.

questions.q: Which caveat belongs in the capstone write-up?
options: The result is guaranteed to hold forever
The confidence interval is wide, the design could reliably detect only about 3.3-point or larger reductions, and 90 days says nothing about longer-term retention
There are no limitations
The p-value proves the effect size is exactly 2.8 points
questions.explain: Honest caveats include interval width, the experiment's detectable effect size, and the limited time window.
